content: Imidazolidinyl urea is an antimicrobial preservative commonly utilized in cosmetic products. It is chemically related to diazolidinyl urea, which serves a similar purpose. Imidazolidinyl urea functions as a formaldehyde-releasing agent. Some individuals may develop a contact allergy to imidazolidinyl urea, which can result in dermatitis. People who are allergic to imidazolidinyl urea often exhibit cross-reactivity and are also allergic to diazolidinyl urea. The chemical structure of imidazolidinyl urea was not well-characterized until recent advancements. It has been discovered that the hydroxymethyl functional group of the imidazolidine ring is attached to a carbon atom rather than a nitrogen atom, contrary to earlier assumptions. The compound still has an incorrect CAS structure assigned to it. Imidazolidinyl urea is synthesized through a chemical reaction between allantoin and formaldehyde in the presence of a sodium hydroxide solution under heat. After the reaction, the mixture is neutralized with hydrochloric acid and subsequently evaporated. The reaction can be summarized as follows: 2 Allantoin + 3 H₂C=O → Imidazolidinyl urea. Commercially available imidazolidinyl urea is not a single compound but rather a mixture of various formaldehyde addition products, including polymers.
